verdict.rationale: Keycloak documents the client credentials grant, which backs service accounts so a non-human client such as an agent can get its own tokens. It pairs this with fine-grained authorization services (resources, role-based policies, a Protection API) and token revocation and introspection, so permissions can be narrowed and credentials revoked. Clients can be created by script through dynamic client registration, the Admin CLI (kcadm.sh) and the Admin REST API. missing for 10: explicit docs on OAuth client-scope configuration and on least-privilege role assignment for service accounts, agent-specific guidance, and independent or hands-on corroboration of this workflow.
